conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas of concern. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it can help us get a sense of how you're adjusting to motherhood.

Please know that everything we discuss today is completely confidential, and I want you to feel safe and supported in sharing your thoughts and feelings with me. My goal is to create a space where you feel comfortable opening up, and I'm here to listen without judgment. 

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and relaxed as possible. 

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like when my baby does something adorable, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and it takes a lot for me to really laugh. Even when I do laugh, it feels kind of forced, like I'm trying to be happy but it's not really genuine. It's hard to explain. I just feel really tired and overwhelmed all the time, and it's hard to find the energy to enjoy things like I used to. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think to myself, "I should be happy right now," but instead, I just feel anxious or worried about something. It's like I'm just pretending to be okay, but inside, I'm not really feeling it. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I don't think I have, not like I used to, anyway. I mean, I've smiled and all, but actually laughing and feeling carefree? That's just not something I've been doing much of lately. To be honest, most of the time I've been feeling pretty down and worried about everything. My baby's safety, my ability to be a good mom... it all just feels really overwhelming. And even when something funny happens, it's hard for me to shake off the worries and just enjoy the moment. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, trying to take care of my baby and keep everything together, but it's all just feeling really tough right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really... I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, it's just been so hard to muster up any enthusiasm. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for walks or reading a book, just don't seem as appealing to me anymore. And with the baby, it's hard to plan anything anyway, because I never know when she'll need to eat or sleep or be changed. It's all just so unpredictable and overwhelming. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, but then I'll just feel anxious about how I'll manage with the baby, or I'll worry that I'm not doing enough for her, and it just feels like too much. So, I don't really look forward to things like I used to. Most of the time, I just feel like I'm trying to get through each day, one task at a time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, actually. I feel like I'm just not doing enough, or that I'm not doing things right, and that everything is my fault. Like, if my baby is crying, I'll think to myself, "If only I had fed her sooner," or "If only I had burped her better." It's like I'm always questioning myself and wondering what I could have done differently. And it's not just with the baby, either. I'll think about things that happened before she was born, and I'll blame myself for not being more prepared, or for not taking better care of myself during pregnancy. It's like I'm just constantly criticizing myself and feeling guilty for everything. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeling really overwhelmed, and I'll just start crying because I feel like I'm just not good enough. It's a really hard feeling to shake, and it makes me feel even more anxious and unsure of myself.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

.. all the time. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something ridiculous, like what if the house catches on fire, or what if someone breaks in. Or I'll worry about my baby's health, like what if she's not gaining enough weight, or what if she's not developing normally. It's like my mind just starts racing and I can't stop thinking about all the things that could go wrong. And it's not just during the day, either. At night, when I'm trying to sleep, my mind will just start racing and I'll lie there for hours, worrying about everything and nothing at the same time. It's exhausting, and it makes me feel like I'm losing my mind. Sometimes I'll be able to calm myself down and remind myself that everything is okay, but other times, the worries just feel overwhelming and I don't know how to make them stop.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just seems to come out of nowhere. And it's not just the feeling of panic that's the problem - it's also the thoughts that come with it. I'll start thinking things like, "What if something happens to my baby?" or "What if I'm not a good enough mother?" And those thoughts just make the panic worse, because I feel like I'm not in control and I don't know what's going to happen. It's a really overwhelming and frightening feeling, and it's hard to shake off once it's started. Sometimes I'll try to distract myself or take some deep breaths, but it's not always easy to calm down when I'm feeling that way.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the house, trying to get some rest... it all just feels so overwhelming. And it's not just the practical things, either. Emotionally, I just feel like I'm drowning. I'll be sitting there, trying to feed the baby or change her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of exhaustion and anxiety wash over me. It's like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, but I'm not sure how much longer I can keep going. Sometimes I'll feel like I'm managing okay, like I've got everything under control, but then something will happen and it'll all just feel like too much again. And the worst part is, I feel like I'm supposed to be able to handle all of this, like I'm supposed to be this perfect, capable mother, but the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and it feels like everything is getting on top of me.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time, although that's definitely part of it. It's more like... I'll be lying there, trying to fall asleep, and my mind just starts racing. I'll think about all the things I need to do, or all the things that could go wrong, and I just can't seem to shut my brain off. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these anxiety dreams or I'll wake up in the middle of the night feeling really overwhelmed and scared. It's like my body is just wired to be "on" all the time, and I don't know how to turn it off. Some nights are better than others, but it's been really hard to get a good night's sleep lately. And when I do get some sleep, I often wake up feeling tired and groggy, like I didn't really rest at all. It's just really frustrating, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but it's just not happening right now.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling any joy or happiness. Everything just feels so overwhelming and exhausting, and I often find myself feeling really sad and miserable. Sometimes it's just a low-grade feeling of sadness, like a cloud is following me around all the time. Other times, it's more intense, and I'll just start crying for no reason. It's like I'm just feeling so much emotion all the time, and I don't know how to process it all. And the worst part is, I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, like I'm supposed to be this happy, glowing new mom. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and it feels like nobody really understands what I'm going through. Sometimes I'll put on a brave face and pretend like everything is okay, but deep down, I'm just feeling really sad and alone. It's a hard feeling to explain, but it's just this constant sense of emptiness and despair, like I'm just not good enough or like I'm failing at this whole mom thing.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just start bawling. Sometimes it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and sometimes it's just because I'm feeling so sad and alone. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll start crying. It's like I'm just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and it's hard to stop once I start. Sometimes I'll cry for hours, just sitting there, feeling so sad and helpless. And it's not just the big things that make me cry, either. Sometimes it's just the little things, like running out of diapers or spilling coffee on my shirt. It's like I'm just so fragile and emotional all the time, and everything sets me off. I've even caught myself crying while I'm nursing the baby, or while I'm rocking her to sleep. It's like my emotions are just right on the surface, and I don't know how to keep them from spilling over all the time. It's really scary, because I feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to get it back.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, struggling to hold back tears) Yes... I'm so ashamed to admit it, but yes, those thoughts have crossed my mind. It's like, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, and I just don't know how to make it stop, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of... of just not being here anymore. It's not like I really want to harm myself, it's just that the pain and the sadness feel so overwhelming, and I don't know how to escape it. It's like my mind is just trying to find a way out, you know? But I know it's not a good way to think, and it scares me. I don't want to hurt myself, I just want to feel better. I want to be a good mom, and I want to be happy, but it feels like everything is just too much for me right now. (starts to cry) I'm so sorry, I don't know why I'm saying this, it's just... it's just really hard for me right now. (sniffles) I don't think I would actually do anything to harm myself, but the thoughts are there, and it's really scary.
